git add src/types/checker/builtin_spl_classes/filesystem.rs tests/codegen/spl.rs tests/codegen/spl/file_object_read_ahead.rs && git -c commit.gpgsign=false commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
fix(spl): SplFileObject's iteration never read ahead, so eof() answered false throughout

php drives its iteration from the STREAM and reads one line ahead of the one it yields, so
`eof()` is already true while the LAST element is still current. elephc iterates a line
ARRAY, whose cursor cannot see the stream, and answered `false` at every step of every
iteration — including the one that had just yielded the final element.

The read-ahead is also what decides whether there IS a trailing empty element. The old rule
tested the last BYTE: a file ending in `\n` gets one more line than `file()` reports,
because after that newline the stream is not yet at end of file. That is a claim about the
STREAM, and one kind of stream disagrees — `php://temp` reports EOF the moment a line read
drains it. MEASURED on `php -n` 8.5.6, `"a\n"` yields TWO elements from a plain file and
ONE from an `SplTempFileObject`; `"a\nb\n"` yields three and two. So the loader takes its
own reading of `feof()`, after the last line ARRIVED rather than after the read that failed
— by then every kind of stream says true.

Reading by hand is the other half of the rule and the reason the stream stays in the
answer: `fgets()` does not read ahead, and two of them over that same plain file leave
`eof()` FALSE. So a hand-driven read takes the object back onto the stream's own answer,
and without that the earlier `rewind()` was still speaking for a cursor the caller had
stopped using — the first `fgets()` of a temp object reported the end of a stream with half
its bytes unread.

Ten rows of the four bodies × both kinds now match php byte for byte, at every step.

`seekState` came along: it was READ by `current()` and `valid()` but only WRITTEN by
`rewind()` and `seek()`, so `(new SplFileObject($p))->current()` — php's own first-line
idiom, with no rewind — died on an uninitialized typed property.
